title: Distributed admission controller with soft-credits for graceful burst absorption
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood has seen repeated short-duration traffic spikes (5–30s) from onboarding customers and bursty inference patterns. Current token-bucket based limiters strictly drop or queue when the bucket is empty, leading to unfair client throttling and brittle failover during limiter outages. We need an approach that absorbs short bursts with minimal client-visible errors while preserving multi-tenant fairness and SLO guarantees across regions.

Proposal summary:
Implement a distributed admission controller that allocates a small pool of "soft-credits" per region and per-customer group. Soft-credits behave as temporary overdraft tokens that can be consumed when a normal quota/token-bucket is exhausted. Consumption of soft-credits increments a fast, local metric and enforces stricter reconciliation over a longer window. Two main axes: (1) local soft-credit pools for low-latency absorption and (2) a global drainage/repayment policy coordinated via an eventually-consistent metadata store to prevent long-term overuse.

Goals / acceptance criteria:
- Reduce client-facing 429/5xx spikes during short bursts by at least 60% in synthetic burst tests.
- Maintain 99th percentile request latency within current SLOs in steady-state and during absorbed bursts.
- Ensure long-running overuse triggers deterministic load-shedding rather than indefinite overdraft.
- Provide observability: per-customer soft-credit utilization, repayment debt, and cross-region reconciliation status.

Design details:
- Admission flow: request arrives -> standard token-bucket check -> if exhausted, consult local soft-credit pool -> if available, grant and mark as overdraft; otherwise apply normal reject/fallback.
- Soft-credit sizing: default per-region pool = 50k tokens (configurable by tier). Credits decay/repay via token regeneration and explicit repayment window (e.g., 10 minutes to 1 hour).
- Fairness: per-tenant proportional caps on soft-credit usage; a fast moving-average weight applied to prevent single tenant drain.
- Multi-region failover: on region evacuation, soft-credit debt is replicated to a global lightweight ledger that other regions can honor as transient debt for controlled period. A fail-open window is carefully bounded to avoid cross-region unbounded consumption.
- Circuit breaker integration: if soft-credit debt crosses a safety threshold or if local limiter is degraded, trigger progressive circuit breaking (probabilistic shedding -> hard-shed) with automatic rollback thresholds.
- State backend: use existing regional metadata store with per-shard leases; design aims to be eventually consistent to keep latency low.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- New metrics: soft_credit_consumed, soft_credit_repaid_rate, soft_credit_debt_by_tenant, soft_credit_overdraft_incidents.
- Dashboards: per-region and per-tier views, alert when debt > 80% of repayment window capacity or when overdraft incidents > 10/minute.
- SLOs to track: 99p latency, 95p error rate during bursts, error budget burn rate for limiter-related errors.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged internal canary in us-west for non-critical tenants (2 weeks).
2) Run synthetic burst tests and inject limiter outages with chaos tests.
3) Gradual expansion to production customers with staged percentage rollout and tight alerting.
4) Enable cross-region ledger only after stable local behavior observed.

Testing:
- Unit tests for admission path and debt accounting.
- Integration tests with token buckets, local pools, and fake metadata store.
- Load tests: 10k parallel clients generating short bursts (5–20s) and measure 429/latency.
- Chaos: simulate metadata store partition, limiter process crash, and region cutover.

Open questions / risks:
- Consistency trade-offs: eventual consistency reduces latency but can allow brief cross-region double-spend; need hard bounds and rate-limiting of cross-region honor.
- Billing/Accounting: how to surface overdraft repayment to billing pipeline and tenant owners.
- Performance overhead: local checks must be <50us added p95 to admission path; need microbenchmarks.
- Policies for tenant-controlled settings (allowing customers to opt-in to overdraft).

Next steps:
- Prototype local pool + admission hook and run benchmark against existing limiter for overhead numbers.
- Design metadata ledger schema and invariants for cross-region reconciliation.
- Schedule design review with Reliability and Product (requested by 2026-03-12).
